title: Lifted external evaluation chain models with common shifted targets
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X,Y,P$ schemes and $a:P\to X$, $b:P\to Y$ morphisms [def-pc-scheme]. Use small etale sites in a common module universe [def-weil-size-convention], ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and direct-sum tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $E,H$ be bounded flat cochain complexes on $X,Y$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Let $I_K,I_L$ be K-injective complexes representing bounded-below objects $K,L$, and suppose $F=a^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}L$ is bounded below [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-kun-derived-tensor]. Write $\underline U_T$ for constant realization [def-kun-constant-sheaf], and $\mathsf H_T(B,M)=R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom_A(B,M))$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Suppose given quasi-isomorphisms of $A$-complexes
$$\alpha:U\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(E,I_K),\qquad\gamma:V\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_Y(H,I_L)$$
with $U,V$ K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Put $t_X(w\otimes e)=\alpha(w)(e)$ and $t_Y(z\otimes h)=\gamma(z)(h)$. Suppose chain maps $u:\underline U_X\otimes_A E\to N_K$, $v:\underline V_Y\otimes_A H\to N_L$, $c_K:N_K\to I_K$ and $c_L:N_L\to I_L$ are given, with $N_K,N_L$ K-flat with flat terms, $c_K,c_L$ quasi-isomorphisms, and $c_Ku\simeq t_X$, $c_Lv\simeq t_Y$. Set $T=a^{-1}N_K\otimes_A b^{-1}N_L$, $G=a^{-1}E\otimes_A b^{-1}H$.

The complex $T$ represents $F$. For every K-injective resolution $i:T\to J$, the formula on local homogeneous sections
$$p(w\otimes z)(e\otimes h)=(-1)^{sq}i\bigl(a^{-1}u(w\otimes e)\otimes b^{-1}v(z\otimes h)\bigr),\quad |w|=r,\ |z|=s,\ |e|=q,$$
defines a chain map $p:U\otimes_A V\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_P(G,J)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Under the canonical identifications of its source with $\mathsf H_X(E,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$ and its target with $\mathsf H_P(G,F)$, its localization is the transpose of the tensor of pulled-back derived evaluations with Koszul interchange. This assertion holds for every choice of the displayed representatives and homotopy lifts, so all give the same derived morphism.

Use $B[1]^q=B^{q+1}$ and $d_{B[1]}=-d_B$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any complex $B$ and K-injective $I$ on one of these sites, the maps
$$\theta_B:\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B[1],I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(B,I)[-1],\qquad(\theta_Bf)^p=(-1)^nf^{p-1}\quad(|f|=n)$$
are chain isomorphisms realizing the first-variable derived Hom shift. The shifted resolution $U[-1]\to\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(E[1],I_K)$ is $\theta_E^{-1}\alpha[-1]$. The formula
$$\eta_{U,E}:\underline{U[-1]}_X\otimes_A E[1]\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline U_X\otimes_A E,\qquad w\otimes e\longmapsto(-1)^r w\otimes e\quad(w\in U[-1]^r)$$
is a chain isomorphism, and the shifted chain evaluation is $t_X\eta_{U,E}$. It is factored up to homotopy by $u\eta_{U,E}$ and the same $c_K,N_K$. The identical assertion holds for $V,H,v$. Consequently the shifted and unshifted external evaluations may all use the same target $T$ and the same $J,i$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-global-hom-evaluation-flat-lift] separately to $(X,E,K,I_K,U,\alpha)$ and $(Y,H,L,I_L,V,\gamma)$. Its hypotheses are exactly the bounded flat sources, bounded-below coefficients, K-injective representatives and flat-term K-flat resolutions assumed here. It identifies the two global Hom complexes with $\mathsf H_X(E,K)$ and $\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$ in $D(A)$, and identifies the localizations of $t_X,t_Y$ with the corresponding derived evaluations. Under localization from the homotopy category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the assumed homotopies give $Q(c_K)Q(u)=Q(t_X)$ and $Q(c_L)Q(v)=Q(t_Y)$. The same cited statement gives K-flatness and flatness of $E,H$ and of the evaluation sources.

source.place: Agent representative refinement of Tags 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), 08J7 (section-internal-hom); evaluation normalization supplied by the cited existing node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the constant-ring morphisms of etale topoi induced by $a,b$. Because their module pullbacks are exact, the ordinary pullbacks of the given flat-term K-flat complexes $E,H,N_K,N_L$ are flat-term K-flat and compute their derived pullbacks. By [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], applied on $P$ to $a^{-1}N_K,b^{-1}N_L$, the complex $T$ is flat-term K-flat and its localization is the derived tensor of their localized objects. The two quasi-isomorphisms $c_K,c_L$ therefore identify $QT$ with $F$. Apply the same tensor-model statement to $a^{-1}E,b^{-1}H$: $G$ is flat-term K-flat and represents $a^{-1}E\otimes_A^Lb^{-1}H$. It is bounded because the degree ranges of $E,H$ have finite sum. Finally apply that statement to $U,V$ viewed as module sheaves on the one-object site with ring $A$: $U\otimes_A V$ is a flat-term K-flat representative of $\mathsf H_X(E,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(H,L)$. Thus $i$ gives the required identification of $QJ$ with $F$.

source.place: Tag 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), together with the representative normalization in the cited node.

proof.text: Write $S=U\otimes_A V$, $C=\underline S_P$, $D_X=a^{-1}(\underline U_X\otimes_A E)$ and $D_Y=b^{-1}(\underline V_Y\otimes_A H)$. Use the canonical constant-pullback and tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-external-evaluation-transpose-natural]. On homogeneous generators their interchange $\chi:C\otimes_A G\to D_X\otimes_A D_Y$ is $(w\otimes z)\otimes(e\otimes h)\mapsto(-1)^{sq}(w\otimes e)\otimes(z\otimes h)$. It is a chain map: after differentiating $w,z,e,h$, the respective coefficients on both sides are $(-1)^{sq}$, $(-1)^{r+sq+q}$, $(-1)^{r+sq}$, $(-1)^{r+q+s+sq}$. Its inverse undoes the permutation with the same Koszul sign. These sectionwise multilinear formulas respect restriction and hence define maps of sheafified tensors and of their direct-sum total complexes. The composite $b=i\circ(a^{-1}u\otimes b^{-1}v)\circ\chi:C\otimes_A G\to J$ is consequently a chain map with exactly the evaluation formula in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes); explicit elementary differential check for the Koszul interchange of the cited external transpose.

proof.text: Curry $b$ on each total-tensor summand, using the product projections defining [def-pur-hom-complex]. For $x=w\otimes z\in S^n$, $n=r+s$, put $p(x)(y)=b(x\otimes y)$ for homogeneous $y=e\otimes h\in G$. Since $b$ is a chain map, $d_Jp(x)(y)=p(d_Sx)(y)+(-1)^n p(x)(d_Gy)$, so $d_{\operatorname{Hom}}p(x)=p(d_Sx)$. Thus $p$ is a chain map. Local bilinearity and sheafification give the sheaf-valued adjunct $\bar p:C\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(G,J)$; degreewise constant/sections adjunction gives precisely the global chain map $p:S\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_P(G,J)$. The formulas are determined on every tensor summand and every Hom-product projection, so no finite-support assertion about Hom products is being assumed. For the separate forward chain-evaluation clause, a map alpha:U→Hom(E,I) gives on each pair of degrees a bilinear presheaf map (w,e)↦alpha(w)(e). The strong monoidality of sheafification and the sheafification adjunction extend this to constant(U^r) tensor E^q→I^(q+r). The monoidal unit identity proves its required formula on constant pure sections and also gives an extensionality principle for such maps. Extend the maps by the native direct-sum tensor universal property. Expanding Mathlib HomComplex.δ_v in the chain-map equation for alpha gives d_I(alpha(w)(e))=alpha(dw)(e)+(-1)^r alpha(w)(d_E(e)). The native ιTensorObj_d formula identifies this with the total-tensor differential. This proves lifted_external_evaluation_chain_evaluation without boundedness, flatness or injectivity assumptions.

source.place: Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose), whose proof reduces to More on Algebra Tag 0A5Y (lemma-compose); the evaluation currying calculation is written out here.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose] hold with its second tensor factor $G$, its K-injective target $J$, and its arbitrary first complex $C$. Therefore the internal derived transpose of $Q(\bar p)$ is $Q(b)$ under the canonical one-sided tensor comparison. Also $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(G,J)$ is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. Apply [lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization] to constant realization left adjoint to sections: its left functor is exact, so all complexes form a resolving class and its left comparison is invertible. On this K-injective target the derived right comparison is invertible, and the cited formula identifies $Q(p)$ with the derived constant/sections adjunct of $Q(\bar p)$. This is the canonical adjunction fixed in [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Combining these normalized transpositions identifies $Q(p)$ with the global derived transpose of $Q(b)$. Since $G$ is bounded flat and $F$ is bounded below, [lem-pur-global-hom-evaluation-flat-lift] on $P$ identifies its target $Q\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_P(G,J)$ with $\mathsf H_P(G,F)$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Tags 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); canonical constant/sections derived adjunction and the cited representative-normalization tool.

proof.text: Under $Q(c_K),Q(c_L)$ the localized lifts are the derived evaluations by step 1. Their pullbacks and tensor are therefore the two pulled-back derived evaluations, because every complex used to compute that tensor is K-flat by steps 1 and 2. The interchange in step 3 is the canonical one, including its $(-1)^{sq}$ sign. It follows that, after the identification $QJ\cong F$ induced by $i$ and $c_K,c_L$, $Q(b)$ is exactly the composite defining the external evaluation transpose in [lem-pur-external-evaluation-transpose-natural]. Step 5 then proves the asserted identity for $Q(p)$. That cited transpose is defined solely from the two derived evaluations and the canonical comparisons; it contains none of the choices $I_K,I_L,U,V,N_K,N_L,J$ or their lifts. Since the argument applies to every choice satisfying the stated hypotheses, the induced derived morphism is independent of all these choices.

source.place: Tags 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat); agent assembly of the displayed augmentation identities, with no tensoring of non-K-flat injective representatives.

proof.text: For the ordinary global cochain complex defined in ExternalRHom, use Mathlib CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain.leftShiftLinearEquiv in degree n-1, with shift 1. Its inverse is leftUnshift, so it gives the degree-n map from Hom(B[1],I) to Hom(B,I)[-1]. The lemma δ_leftUnshift says that applying the unshifted Hom differential contributes the sign 1.negOnePow. This cancels the sign (-1).negOnePow in the differential of the shifted target. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents therefore assembles these linear equivalences into a chain isomorphism. The displayed leftUnshift normalization is definitional. This construction works for every pair B,I; the existing K-injectivity hypothesis is not needed for this chain-level clause. The identification with the derived first-variable shift remains the separate final clause and uses the normalized Hom models and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Tag 08J7 (section-internal-hom); explicit agent sign calculation for the source shift.

proof.text: For $w\in U[-1]^r$, $e\in E[1]^q$, view $w,e$ in original degrees $r-1,q+1$. Applying $\eta$ to the source differential gives $(-1)^r dw\otimes e-w\otimes de$. This is also $d((-1)^rw\otimes e)$ in $\underline U_X\otimes E$, by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Thus $\eta$ is a chain map. The inverse uses the same sign on the corresponding summand, so it is a chain isomorphism. The shifted quasi-isomorphism $\alpha'=\theta_E^{-1}\alpha[-1]$ has value $\alpha'(w)(e)=(-1)^r\alpha(w)(e)$; consequently its chain evaluation is exactly $t_X\eta$, not merely an unspecified derived comparison. The sign depends only on the degree of the $U[-1]$ factor, so these formulas respect sheafification and restriction. The same calculation with $V,H$ gives the second shifted evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes); explicit elementary shift and tensor differential calculation.

proof.text: Shifting a complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms, since $H^n(C[-1])=H^{n-1}(C)$. It preserves flat terms and K-flatness: for any acyclic complex $D$, the chain isomorphism $D\otimes U[-1]\cong(D\otimes U)[-1]$, $x\otimes w\mapsto(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes w$, makes the defining acyclicity test identical [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Thus $U[-1],\alpha'$ satisfy the shifted hypotheses, and $E[1]$ remains bounded flat. If $k$ is the given degree-$-1$ homotopy with $c_Ku-t_X=dk+kd$, then $k\eta$ gives $c_K(u\eta)-t_X\eta=d(k\eta)+(k\eta)d$ because $\eta$ is a chain map. Hence $u\eta$ lifts the shifted evaluation through the same $N_K,c_K$. The identical computation for $v$ gives the same $N_L,c_L$. Neither operation changes $T=a^{-1}N_K\otimes b^{-1}N_L$, so the original $i:T\to J$ is a K-injective resolution for each shifted construction as well. Applying the preceding steps to either or both shifted inputs proves the common-target assertion.
